about: At “Nobis quoque peccatóribus” the rubric directs the priest to raise his voice a little and strike his breast. The prayer asks that God's sinful servants be admitted to fellowship with the Saints.

s01.narrative: The priest strikes his breast with his right hand and says, with his voice raised a little:

s02.translation: To us, also, Your servants, who, though sinners,

s03.narrative: The priest spreads his hands as before and goes on silently.

s04.translation: hope in Your abundant mercies, graciously grant some share and fellowship with Your holy Apostles and Martyrs:

s05.translation: with John the Baptist, Stephen, Matthias, Barnabas, Ignatius, Alexander, Marcellinus, Peter, Felicity, Perpetua, Agatha, Lucy, Agnes, Cecilia, Anastasia and all Your Saints:

s06.translation: admit us, we beseech You, into their company, not weighing our merits, but granting us Your pardon.

w001.function: Dative governed by “donáre” (w015), placed at the head of the petition.

w002.function: Links this petition to the preceding commemoration of the dead.

w010.function: The participle agrees with “Nobis” (w001) and “fámulis” (w004): it is we who hope.

w031.function: Peter the Exorcist, companion of Marcellinus, not the Apostle.

w058.function: No Amen follows. The sentence continues with Per quem hæc ómnia.
